# tiny-route-redact

## What it is
Middleware that redacts credentials from route paths so logs, error reports, and observability spans never leak them.

## When to use it
- Any HTTP service that logs request paths.
- Any service that emits trace spans with the `http.path` attribute.
- Any service that ships error reports to Sentry / Datadog / Honeycomb with the request path included.
- Any service that exposes a `/metrics` endpoint that includes the request path.

## When NOT to use it
- Body redaction - use `tiny-secret-mask` v0.2.0 `mask_json` instead.
- Trace context redaction - use `tiny-secret-mask` v0.3.0 `mask_trace_context` instead.
- Log message redaction - use `tiny-log` v0.5.x + `tiny-secret-mask`.

## Public API (one-liner each)
- `redact_path(path)` - returns the redacted path string.
- `route_redactor_middleware(get_response, *, stats, on_redact)` - WSGI-style middleware.
- `route_redactor_asgi_middleware(app, *, stats)` - ASGI-style middleware.
- `RedactionStats` - counter object for `/metrics` endpoints.

## Dependencies
- `tiny-secret-mask >= 0.4.0` (auto-installed).
- Python 3.8+.
- No other runtime dependencies.
